Rin's character question is how a person who can keep a damaged administration working can retain a life that competent service does not exhaust. Her repertoire contains public explanation, coordination, refused coercion, investigation and technical reliance. It also contains wanted meals, films, games, rest, an old friend's company, a first chess loss and a continuing inquiry that no successful outing finishes. Those ordinary ends are substantial parts of the person. Reading them only as techniques for returning a useful official to work would reproduce the very reduction the material puts under pressure. The stronger thesis is that Rin repeatedly tries to distinguish an answerable obligation from an unlimited demand. In the Prologue, exceptional access to Schale has a situated administrative purpose. In Final, she contributes to a distributed response whose capacity belongs to many students, systems and particular decisions. In the later locally ordered rest and inquiry accounts, she can accept food and play while returning to a question that remains unresolved. Neither refusal nor pleasure guarantees a finished institutional repair. Each prevents capability from becoming the whole criterion of a person's value. [M0; M4; F; S0; S1]
